README: The sound sheet: which music, which air and which effect, tied to cues and words, never to seconds. Rules: Topics/InThisTown/SOUND.md. Build: python3 scripts/sound.py build in-this-town-nobody-looked-at-the-moon

sections.why: Hook, the three things nobody knew, and the tour: a town that is up all night, and busy with it.
A good life with one thing in it you may not look at. He asks, and gets half a rule and no reason.
First try: straight up. The town's answer is a bucket. Oom-pah.
Second try: the other way. Thirty nights of pushing a stone while nobody looks. One plucked bass, on tiptoe.
The edge: the last shove, one look back, the hat off, the lean. A pulse that grows for nine seconds.
It cuts off on the cut to the water. No music for 3.9 seconds: drops, and then the first blink, alone.
It was an eye, and it has caught him. One low note.
Something is finally looking at him, and he waves at it. The music believes him. It is as wrong as he is.
The wheat behind him has gone dark. No music for 2.1 seconds: only wood, and a riser, into the worst line of the film.
The scarecrows were walking. The low note comes back and does not move.
What the stare was for, and what the nights were for. He understands it now. Slow broken chords.
Under his hat, seeing nothing, waiting for it to get bored: one low note and air, and steps coming.
It knows him now. Back to the low note, with a heartbeat on top, to the end. It does not turn cheerful for the subscribe line.

beds.why: The whole film is one night after another, out of doors: crickets and still air.
A town that is awake all night: voices, no words.
Wind is the sound of the fields. Every shot out there has it.
Looking down the well: a low rumble and a drip. The town is behind him and he has stopped hearing it.
The last of it. Every door shuts in 11.light, and the voices never come back: from there on the town is silent.
The wheat, and what is walking out of it.

sfx.why: The town bell: the moon is up, so the town gets up. It rings three times in the film: here, quietly when the bell ringer is named (5.ask), and for the watch at the fence, when he understands what it was for (13.awake).
Something very big comes up behind his roof.
The moonlight has a sound, and this is it: small, high and cold. Planted here. It is on the wheat (3.light), under his brim (7.edge), in the well (11.moon), and then in town (11.light).
His own hand pulls the brim down. Straw is the sound of the hats, all film.
The brim comes down like a shutter: the rule, in one sound. Paid back at 13.hat.
Scene 2: the three things nobody knew.
The board with the rule on it.
Two children chase each other past the well, in step: a landing every 0.2645 s from 0.13 s (scene2: 2.2 m a second; a villager is at full stride every 0.58 m).
All night: a clock that is not there.
Out past the fence.
Dry wood: the sound of the scarecrows. Planted here, on the word. It comes back each time one is nearer, and it is the last sound of the film.
Wheat.
Scene 3: the tour. Straight down on the square.
Straw: the hats, sliding round each other.
Eight pairs of feet under eight hats. From up here that is all the town is.
The cut to the golem from below, as big as a house: its weight, on the cut. (Not a footfall: at 0.4 m a second its foot does not land inside this shot.)
Iron is the golem's sound.
Its hat.
Three pairs of feet come down together: all three are at full stride 0.58 s in (scene3: walk = 0.5 t).
Brim meets brim (scene3: BUMPED = 'bumped' + 0.1).
Both step the same way round, and bump again (scene3: AGAIN).
A slab you could not lift with a horse.
The bucket on its hook, swinging. Planted: it is the bucket of 7.bucket.
The moon, over his roof.
Water, under the stone. Planted: the next drops are in 10.gap and 11.moon.
The fly up the lane, out of the lantern light.
The golem on its rounds along the fence: full stride at 1.16 and 2.70 s into this shot (world: walk = 0.85 × the film's seconds).
The white on the wheat: the moonlight's sound, where it lives.
The dry wood again, close.
The push at the black between the trunks.
Nothing ever came out. One of them is standing half in the trees.
Scene 4: the bench under his window.
She leans her hat on his.
A quiet life, and a good one.
His head goes back as far as it dares.
The question.
Scene 5: the bell ringer, up on the step of her bell.
Her bell, the second time: quiet, the way you hear it standing under it.
His arm goes straight up at the thing he is asking about.
Her brim comes up, a little.
She speaks. It is the most anybody here has ever said.
She bends down to his ear, brim over brim.
The rule's other half.
The brim comes down like a shutter.
She steps off her stone: full stride at 0.73 and 0.92 s (scene5: walk = 1.4 * down).
And goes, up the street: 1.2 m a second, a stride every 0.485 s (scene5: gone).
Scene 6.
He shrugs at the whole idea.
Up the lane behind him, the one by the track is nearer than it was. Nobody says so. The wood does.
Decided.
His hand finds the brim.
He has decided. A small rise into the next night.
The golem comes down the lane behind him: full stride at 0.35 and 0.80 s (scene7: walk = 2.2 * arrive).
The hat goes back.
Nothing between his face and the sky.
The white comes in under the straw (scene7: on 'one', all there by 'white'). The moonlight's sound, nearer than it has ever been.
The golem.
Its arm comes over him, as slow as a crane (scene7: 0 to 0.85 s).
It lets go.
The bucket lands on his head (scene7: LANDS).
His hat comes down again, on top of the bucket.
He finds the post of the rule board with his head.
They knock on it with their noses: one on 'knocked' (scene7: KNOCK_1)...
...and one after it (KNOCK_2 = 'on' + 0.06).
Scene 8: the other way.
His eyes go one way (scene8: at 0.57 s)...
...and the other (0.9 s). Nobody.
He grins.
Stone on stone: three heaves, on 'every', 'pushed' and 'further' (kit: slabAt).
From high up: the rail under the slab, and it gives, at 0.5 and 1.4 s (kit: slabAt).
Even the golem walks past: full stride at 0.93 s (scene8: walk = 0.7 t).
A scratch for every night: the count, going up.
The last one is cut.
Scene 9: the last night.
His own steps, coming up to the well: 0.34, 0.66 and 0.95 s (scene9: 2.35 m, eased, over 1.4 s; the walk clip plants a foot every 0.71 m). He is under the lens: heard, not seen.
Her head comes up.
She slides off the lid...
...and lands beside the well (scene9: 0.42 s later).
Her brim comes up, and for one second she looks at him.
She turns right round.
Scene 10: the last shove.
The slab grinds the last hand's width (kit: slabAt, from 'gap' to 0.25 s after 'just').
It stops.
A black slot, and water at the bottom of it.
He looks over his shoulder, and the lens goes where he looks.
Lantern flames.
A door standing open, with a kitchen in it. Everything he has. They shut at 11.light.
Not one of them tips.
The hat lifts clear.
The first bare head this town has seen in years.
Two sleeves come down flat on the stone (scene10: they are down 0.1 s after 'hands').
He leans over. It ends on the cut, and so does the music.
No music. Water, a long way down.
There it is: the thing nobody is allowed to see.
The water shivers (scene11: on 'shaking').
THE BLINK. Two lids shut over the moon and open again (scene11: blinkAt BLINKED, shut for 0.1 s). The film's own sound: three more in 13.blink, and one in each of the last three shots.
It was an eye.
The iris goes round the white, the long way (scene11: from 0.16 s to 'and').
It stops dead in the middle, on us. The frame jumps (scene11: impacts).
Up out of the well.
His head goes back, all the way, with no hat on it.
Over his roof the moon is an eye, and it is looking at him.
The town goes by with its brims down.
What the moon sees: down out of the sky at one face, turned up.
He waves at it: the arm is up by 'looking', and it swings every half second (the wave clip).
Something was finally looking at him. It is the best thing that ever happened to him.
The white comes off the wheat and down the lane like a tide (kit: 0.2 to 2.25 s).
The moonlight's sound, in town, for the first time.
Every hat in the square runs for a door: six of them, from 'moonlight' to the end of the shot (scene11: run).
Every door shuts (kit: 0.1 s before 'came').
Scene 12: him, in the cold white.
Wind, from the fields behind him.
No music. The wheat has gone dark.
The dry wood. All of them.
The first steps (kit: the march begins on 'begun'; marcher 0 is at full stride 0.35 s later, marcher 2 at 1.71 s, marcher 1 at 2.03 s). A scarecrow's foot is a stick: this is its sound.
The only thing that rises in 12.dark. It ends on the cut.
The scarecrows were walking. The one boom of the film, on the cut to the first one seen walking.
It comes straight at the lens: full stride at 0.40 and 0.90 s (kit: marcher 1).
Scene 13: some night long ago, at the edge of the trees.
One of them steps out of the black on its own two legs: full stride at 0.20, 0.59 and 0.98 s (scene13: walk = 1.9 t).
One blink at a time: three blinks. The lids meet at 0.49, 1.07 and 1.65 s (kit: WALK_BLINKS, each shut 0.07 s after it begins)...
...and in the dark of each, seven of them take one step: the feet are down 0.2 s after the blink begins (scene13).
From out in the wheat, behind them.
Held.
The stare is the light.
The bell, the third time: this is what it was for.
All night, every night: the clock of 2.awake. Now we know what it was counting.
Back at the well. They are coming.
The hat comes down, right down, over his eyes.
Behind him in the lane: the nearest one is at full stride at 0.17 and 0.88 s (kit: marcher 0).
The shutter of 1.look. This time he wants it shut.
Under the hat.
Nearer (kit: marcher 0, the one the lens is behind, at 0.28 and 0.99 s; marcher 1, beside the lens, at 0.40, 0.90 and 1.40 s).
Its lid sinks and the iris drifts off, from 0.3 to 1.35 s (kit): the sound it made when it rolled (11.caught).
Kit: marcher 0 at 0.10 and 0.81 s.
The white goes back up the lane the way it came (kit: 0.1 to 1.08 s).
The last step. On 'stopped' every one of them is a scarecrow again.
He lifts the brim to see.
One arm's length away.
Scene 14: the eye, filling the frame.
It finds his house.
It blinks (kit: LAST_BLINKS, shut for 0.16 s)...
...and in the dark each of them takes one step: the feet are down 0.24 s after the blink begins (kit).
One step. Nearer, so louder.
The red sign.
The subscribe line gets the one clean bell note of the film.
Before it blinks again: it blinks.
The step that puts one at his shoulder.
The last sound of the film: its head goes slowly over on one side (kit: from 'again', 0.45 s). The dry wood of 2.crows.
